earlier_findings.note: communicate(input=...) in a per-worker thread; verified on 3.12.14: 5 MiB request delivered, 1 MiB stdout + 3 MiB stderr drained, rc 0/5/-9 correct, terminate kills and joins. Residual minor N1 (pipe error before wait() hangs).
Chain always required for v3 generation>=1; length==generation, first==original_claim, last==previous_claim; P or C0 as previous_claim at generation 2 refused.
Each chain commit adds one regular canonical consumption record of a v3 request of the same attempt/publication at that generation. Residual minor N4.

Binding resolved: start_sha256 and generation_claim in entry; start record schema/match/manifest/edition/512/claim commit/attempt re-checked; saved row claim must be an ancestor of current claim. Replay accepted (design scope). Residual minor N3 (ancestry broader than chain).
Result-file failure halts dispatch via stop_index; interrupt re-raised immediately; row status no longer overwritten.
stop_index lets lower running rows save in order; finish/dispatch catch only Exception so interrupts reach the handler that terminates all running workers. Residual minor N2.
Pipes drained concurrently; no hang with 3 MiB stderr.

results_ref may be None for generation>=1 only with 0 rows and an absent branch; operator prevalidate/consume re-verify the results reference before consumption. Residual minor N5 (chain not checked pre-consumption).
Per-generation workspace results-<attempt>-gNNN, detached worktrees only, workspace inside repository refused (before destination mkdir).
No runtime change; justification (canonical manifest-derived states, equivalence test) holds.
Cache key covers catalog, fixture and every referenced rules file hash; ~1.8 ms per hit, informational only.

findings.summary: _Worker.poll() returns None forever if communicate() raised before wait(): the recorded pipe error is never surfaced
findings.failure_scenario: A non-BrokenPipe OSError inside _communicate on the lowest row leaves returncode None; poll() stays None, finish() is never called, supervisor sleeps indefinitely without a stop record (reproduced with communicate patched to raise). Hang, not a wrong result; practically unreachable on Linux.

findings.summary: Interrupt during verification of the row being finished leaves it 'started' with no result file; narrow leak window between _launch and running[index] in dispatch (line 253)
findings.failure_scenario: KeyboardInterrupt during edition.verify/_verify_row: row already popped from running, so the outer handler does not record it; nothing counted. An interrupt exactly after _launch returns leaves one child untracked.

findings.summary: Saved-row claim check uses merge-base ancestry (accepts publication P and all prior history) and does not bind generation_claim.comment_id or resume_generation to the chain position (ledger _start_bindings line 77-85)
findings.failure_scenario: A self-consistent forged row on the results branch whose generation_claim.commit and start.json binding name P passes resume verification; requires results-branch push access and is within the accepted no-replay scope.

findings.summary: Chain record checks looser than the claim's own checks: filename via isdigit/int (leading zeros, non-ASCII digits), record key set not exact, embedded approval not re-checked with _check_saved_approval, previous_claim linkage between records not checked
findings.failure_scenario: A hand-made chain commit with a fabricated but schema-valid record passes the structure check for a later generation; the later generation is still live-approved for that exact previous_claim and no row can have run under the fabricated claim.

findings.summary: Claim chain / generation-number validity is checked only after the claim exists (_read_committed_claim), not in prevalidate/consume
findings.failure_scenario: Operator passes a wrong generation (e.g. 2 with previous_claim=C0 after an unpublished generation-1 consumption); owner approves, consume writes the claim, run then fails 'chain length differs from the generation'. Fail-closed but the approval is spent.
